newsitem.title: USA: Two found guilty of peddling false Japanese bonds.
newsitem.headline: Two found guilty of peddling false Japanese bonds.

text.p: A Japanese and an American man were found guilty by a federal jury on Monday of trying to sell a counterfeit $500 million Japanese bond.
The jury found Yuji Hitomi and Douglas Wright guilty on three counts of conspiracy, including wire fraud, and a fourth count of trying to sell the bond.
Another Japanese man, Motohichi Muto, pleaded guilty to the charges last Monday, when the trial of all three men began.
Federal prosecutors said Muto brought the counterfeit bonds into the United States in 1993 and that Hitomi and Wright worked with him in the scheme.
The three were first arrested in September 1993, but Muto fled the United States for Japan while out on bail. He was later flown back to South Carolina on March 13.
Jurors deliberated for three hours and found Hitomi and Wright guilty on all four counts on Monday night.
Federal Judge Charles Simmons jailed Hitomi until his Japanese passport could be located. Wright was set free, having posted bond when arrested.
The three men face up to 10 years in prison and $250,000 in fines each.
Lawyers for both defendants said they would appeal the conviction.
